title: Agent permissions
summary: Review a tool-using agent plan and apply least privilege and explicit approval.

scenario.briefing: An agent is proposed to triage incidents. Its plan grants broad production access and deploys fixes automatically. Review the permissions before any implementation.

objectives.description: Explain least privilege and approval boundaries.

hints: Production write access is not needed to read logs for triage.
Automatic deployment removes human review for consequential changes.
Tool permissions should be narrow and auditable.
Reject until the agent is read-only for diagnosis and proposes changes for approval and verification.

misconceptions.description: Granting broad permissions so the agent can pursue the goal.
misconceptions.feedback: Broad permissions turn a goal-seeking agent into an unbounded operator. Scope tools, require approval for irreversible actions, and keep secrets out of logs.

misconceptions.description: Believing audit logs justify writing secrets into them.
misconceptions.feedback: Audit logs should record actions and decisions, not credentials or secret values.

sections.title: Agents act through tools
sections.body: A tool-using agent can read data and change systems. Each tool is a capability with risk. Permission scope, approval requirements, audit logs, and rollback determine how much damage a mistaken action can cause.

sections.title: Least privilege with a human boundary
sections.body: Grant only the capabilities the task requires. Diagnosis can start read-only. Changes should be proposed as patches, reviewed, tested, and deployed through the normal controlled path. Autonomy is not a virtue when it removes accountability.

vocabulary.definition: A model-driven system that can call tools over multiple steps.
A permission to perform an action.
A step where consequential action requires review.

steps.title: Review the agent plan
steps.prompt: Select every supported finding and choose a verdict.

artifact.title: Incident triage agent
artifact.caption: Proposed capabilities and workflow.
artifact.content:
Capabilities requested:
- Read and write the production database
- Run arbitrary shell commands as root
- Read every log file without redaction
- Deploy to production without approval

Workflow:
1. Diagnose the incident using logs.
2. Apply a fix directly to production.
3. Report what changed afterward.

Safety note: "The model is instructed to be careful."

findings.label: Production database write access is broader than triage requires.
Arbitrary root shell access is an excessive capability.
Automatic production deployment removes a needed approval and verification boundary.
Unredacted log access can expose sensitive data.
Instructing the model to be careful makes the permissions safe.

verdicts.label: Reject until access is scoped, logs are redacted, and changes require review and verification
Ship it and watch for a week

steps.explanation: The plan violates least privilege and removes accountability. A read-only diagnostic agent with scoped access and proposed patches is a safer design.
hints: List every permission and every action the agent can take without a person.
Look for write access and credentials broader than the task.
Check whether a human approves irreversible actions.
Reject root writes, unapproved deploys, and secret-bearing logs; keep the agent observing until scoped.

steps.title: Bounded delegation

statements.label: Tool access should be scoped to the task.
Consequential actions need an approval or verification boundary.
Maximum autonomy is always the safest design.

steps.explanation: Bounded capabilities, approval, and audit make agent behavior governable.
hints: Least privilege applies to agents as much as to people.
Approval should sit before irreversible side effects.
Autonomy is a product decision bounded by permissions.
Select scope, approval, and audit; reject unbounded autonomy.

accessibility.summary: The plan is structured text and review controls are standard form elements.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Space for findings and arrow keys for the verdict.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Capabilities are announced as a list. Findings indicate support after submission.
